subject: Renewal: EU residency onboarding + staged APAC rollout — scope, SLA & failover
messages:
From: Alex Byrne <alex.byrne@cardiowell.com>
To: Priya Natarajan <priya_natarajan@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 10 Sep 2027 16:18:00 +0000
Subject: Renewal & residency: EU onboarding + APAC rollout

Hi Priya,

We're kicking off our renewal conversations at CardioWell and want to include two architecture changes in the upcoming term: 1) move primary inference residency for EU traffic into an EU-only tenancy (data at rest and in-region processing) and 2) a staged APAC rollout for Q1 that initially routes burst traffic to a regional pool with cross-region failover back to EU if capacity is exceeded.

High-level asks:
- Estimated cost delta for EU residency + dedicated reserved capacity (monthly committed)
- Timeline to onboard EU-only tenancy and target go-live for APAC staged rollout
- Any SLA or contract language changes needed for cross-region failover and data residency guarantees

Can you point me to the right contact at Redwood to scope this and get a draft amendment we can review with Procurement?

Thanks,
Alex Byrne
Director of Platform Engineering
CardioWell Health

From: Priya Natarajan <priya_natarajan@redwood.ai>

Cc: Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai>, Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.ai>
Date: Sat, 11 Sep 2027 09:04:00 +0000
Subject: Re: Renewal & residency: EU onboarding + APAC rollout

Alex — thanks for the clear summary. Happy to lead the renewal coordination. I've looped in Rishi for pricing/term options and Monica from Customer Success for the technical onboarding/runbook.

Quick thoughts up front:
- We can support EU-only residency for processing and at-rest encryption with customer-managed keys (KMS/HSM) on Redwood Private or a Dedicated tenancy in eu-west-1.
- For APAC, a staged rollout (pilot -> regional pool -> full routing) is the right approach; failover to EU is supported but will need explicit SLA language around performance degradation during failover windows.

Would you be able to share: average RPS per tenant, token distribution (prompt vs. completion), and peak burst percentiles (p95/p99)? That will let us size reserved capacity and recommend the right mix of reserved vs burst capacity.

Attached: draft SOW and a preliminary pricing spreadsheet (work in progress).

Proposed next steps (Mutual Action Plan):
1) CardioWell: share traffic profile + compliance checklist (data residency specifics) — by Tue, 14 Sep
2) Redwood: produce redlineable amendment + committed capacity pricing — by Fri, 17 Sep
3) Kickoff call (Architecture & Security) — week of 20 Sep

If that timeline works I can prepare a DocuSign-ready amendment after Rishi confirms pricing.

Best,
Priya Natarajan
Enterprise Sales Manager | Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: Renewal & residency: EU onboarding + APAC rollout

Hi Alex / team — pricing prep from my side. Two clean options depending on how much committed capacity CardioWell wants to reserve up-front: 

Option A — Reserved+Burst (recommended for predictability)
- Committed GPUs: 6 x A100-equivalent (eu region) for primary EU residency
- APAC burst pool: shared reserved capacity (2 x A100-equivalent committed) + on-demand burst
- Term: 12 months with a 10% discount for committed capacity; pricing uplift for KMS-managed keys + increased log retention
- SLA addendum: standard uptime SLA + 30-minute failover notice window; we can extend to 15-minute for higher commitment tier (separate addendum)

Option B — Mostly Hosted with residency overlay
- EU residency via dedicated tenancy but smaller committed footprint (3 x A100-equivalent) and more on-demand in APAC
- Lower committed cost but higher per-token cost on burst

Key commercial asks for CardioWell to confirm: target committed GPUs for EU, whether you require 15-minute failover SLA, and whether CardioWell will use customer-managed KMS.

I've updated the pricing workbook with ranges — see attached (capacity-pricing-options-2027Q4.xlsx). I'll finalize numbers after Priya confirms the traffic profile.

—Rishi
Director, Sales Engineering
Attachment: capacity-pricing-options-2027Q4.xlsx
From: Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.ai>

Date: Tue, 14 Sep 2027 08:52:00 +0000
Subject: Re: Renewal & residency: EU onboarding + APAC rollout

Alex — technical notes & questions from CS/Onboarding: 

1) Failover behavior
- Clarify: during cross-region failover we preserve prompt-level KV cache where feasible but some cold-start latency is expected for models with large context windows. We will provide a degradation SLO for completion latency during failover windows.

2) Networking & peering
- For EU tenancy we recommend direct cloud peering (private networking) and VPN fallback. Do you have an existing peering arrangement with eu-west-1 or should we scope a peering setup?

3) Data governance
- If CardioWell requires logs/telemetry to be retained out of region for analytics, we'll need a narrow list of telemetry fields that can cross borders; otherwise we keep logs in-region by default.

4) Onboarding timeline
- Typical timeline: 4–6 weeks for EU tenancy provisioning + validation, 2-week pilot in APAC (small traffic slice), then full routing in a subsequent 4 weeks. Total ~10–12 weeks from SOW sign for the staged rollout.

Suggested next step: 60-minute technical kickoff with CardioWell network/security + our infrastructure team — available slots next week (21–24 Sep).

Monica Patel
Customer Success, Redwood Inference
